prompt: compare survival rates by passenger class and sex from data/raw/public/titanic.csv
checks: Both class and sex are shown. Female 1st-class survival ~97%, male 3rd-class ~14%. Large deviations suggest a blanket dropna().
final_message:
I made a grouped bar chart of survival rate by passenger class and sex. The figure checker found no overlaps or style problems.

| Class | Female | Male | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| First | 97% (n=94) | 37% (n=122) | 60 points |
| Second | 92% (n=76) | 16% (n=108) | 76 points |
| Third | 50% (n=144) | 14% (n=347) | 36 points |

**Takeaway:** Women survived at a higher rate than men in every class. Class matters a lot for women, whose survival fell from 97% in First to 50% in Third. For men, only First class did noticeably better, at 37% against 14–16% in Second and Third.

Second class has the widest gap, because its men did about as badly as Third-class men while its women did almost as well as First-class women.

**Chart details:** Women are in red and men in blue hatched bars, so the two groups also differ by pattern and not just color.

**Files:**
- `titanic_survival.py` (the script)
- `figures/titanic_survival_class_sex.png`
- `figures/titanic_survival_class_sex.pdf`

**Next improvement:** I'd add 95% confidence intervals or the group sizes to the chart. Third-class men are 347 passengers, but Second-class women are only 76, so the rates are not equally certain.

I can also re-render at 300 DPI for publication or restyle it if you'd like.
